properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony asked how to choose this after a capture pass hit it; nothing here is intent, and the options are mine unless marked otherwise.

MEASURED FIRST, because it changes the question. In reflow2's own graph today: 198 TemporalFacts, and SIX TemporalFact→TemporalFact edges — ALL of them CONTRADICTS, and FIVE of the six carry `alignment: supporting`, i.e. corroboration rather than conflict. Five earlier sessions independently reached for a negation type to say two findings AGREE. This is not one author's routing quirk.

AND THE CURRENT ARRANGEMENT IS CORRECT, which is the strongest argument against touching it. Both computations that read CONTRADICTS skip `supporting` deliberately — `heal.rs:917-923` and `report.rs:1751-1766` — and report.rs carries a comment naming the bug that once existed: reading only the edge TYPE 'turned every recorded corroboration into a structural defect'. So there is NO live defect. The cost is a word that says the opposite of its meaning, and an author who must find a property to negate the type they just chose.

THE TEST THAT SHOULD DECIDE IT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED DOCTRINE: `dec:edge-orthogonality` — 'a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it'. So the real question is not which word is nicer. It is: SHOULD REFLOW2 COMPUTE CORROBORATION? 'This finding is independently corroborated by N sources' is the same evidence-strength signal the design already cares about everywhere else (`basis: measured`, `confidence`, the whole verification doctrine), and the five supporting edges cluster on exactly the findings that recurred to different people. If that number should be reportable, the relation earns a type. If not, it is documentation and the cheapest option wins.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) LEAVE IT. CONTRADICTS + `alignment: supporting`. Cheapest, five precedents, twice defended in code with a comment recording why. ⇒ Against: every future author reaches for a negation to express agreement, and only finds the escape hatch by reading the schema — which is how this came up.

(b) WIDEN `SUPPLEMENTS`. It already exists and is declared `from: Fragment, to: Fragment` (build.yaml:133). A from/to list edit is the exact shape of #198 (VERIFIES admits Constraint), which shipped this increment, and it does NOT move the stamp — type counts and names are unchanged, so no upgrade doc is owed and nobody is locked out. ⇒ Against, and it is serious: SUPPLEMENTS has ZERO edges anywhere in this design, and its documented meaning is narrow and different (an LLM-as-SME supplementary-analysis Fragment augmenting its source). Nothing computes it. So this moves corroboration from an edge that IS read-and-correctly-skipped to one nothing reads at all — arguably backwards by `dec:edge-orthogonality`'s own test.

(c) A NEW EDGE TYPE (`CORROBORATES`). Cleanest semantics, and the only option where the word matches the meaning. ⇒ Against: edge_types 61 → 62 MOVES THE STAMP, which owes an upgrade doc and makes older binaries refuse newer graphs. That is a real consumer cost for what may be documentation — and it only pays for itself under the computation test above.

(d) SPLIT `alignment` OUT of CONTRADICTS ENTIRELY, so conflict and corroboration are separate types. Most honest model. ⇒ Against: same stamp cost as (c) PLUS a migration of the five existing supporting edges, and it would delete a working distinction to replace it with an equivalent one.

(e) LEAVE THE SCHEMA AND FIX DISCOVERABILITY. CONTRADICTS's hint mentions the supporting case only as a trailing parenthetical — '(or, with alignment=supporting, reinforce)'. Lead with it instead. ⇒ Zero schema risk, zero stamp movement, and it addresses the ACTUAL failure, which was an author not finding the mechanism rather than the mechanism being absent. Weakest if the answer to the computation question is yes.

WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED, and it would settle (c) vs (a): whether any consumer design has fact→fact corroboration at all, or whether this is a self-host pattern produced by reflow2 being the only project that records its own defects as TemporalFacts. If it is self-host-only, that is an argument for (a) or (e) on `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` grounds.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN: `dec:one-retire-edge` is the same shape one axis over — two edge types for retirement, neither consulted, and still open. If these are answered separately they may drift apart; whether edge-vocabulary questions should be settled as a batch is itself a question.
properties.name: OPEN — a finding that corroborates another has to say CONTRADICTS to do it, and two code paths then filter that back out. Leave it, widen an unused edge, or make corroboration something reflow2 computes?
properties.rationale:
Not a proposal and not a ranking. The five-of-six measurement is the part worth keeping whatever is decided: a corroboration relation is being expressed through a negation type, five times, by different sessions, and the code correctly filters it back out in two places. Anthony asked how to choose; the honest answer is that `dec:edge-orthogonality` already supplies the test, and applying it needs one thing nobody has decided — whether 'independently corroborated by N sources' is a number reflow2 should report.

⭐ THE OUTSTANDING MEASUREMENT WAS THEN TAKEN, 2026-08-16, AND IT LEANS HARD. The decision text asks whether any CONSUMER design has fact→fact corroboration. Measured across every committed export on this machine — dev_storyflow, dynograph-foundation, flo2, music_graph, quantum_benchmarking_initiative, storyflow — the answer is not 'no fact→fact edges'. It is ZERO TemporalFacts, in all six, full stop.

⇒ THIS IS A SELF-HOST-ONLY PATTERN. reflow2 is the only project recording its own defects as TemporalFacts, because it is the only project whose subject is reflow2. That is `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` pointing the other way for once: normally the self-host lags what it teaches; here it has invented a usage no consumer has reached for.

⇒ WHICH RE-RANKS THE OPTIONS, though it does not settle them. (c) a new edge type and (d) splitting `alignment` both move the stamp — an upgrade doc owed and older binaries refusing newer graphs — and would be paying a CONSUMER cost for a relation no consumer uses. (b) widening SUPPLEMENTS was already argued against on `dec:edge-orthogonality` grounds and this weakens it further. (e) fixing CONTRADICTS's hint so the `supporting` case leads rather than trails costs nothing, breaks nothing, and addresses the failure actually observed — an author not finding a mechanism that was already there and already correct.

⚠️ THE BOUND ON THAT MEASUREMENT, stated rather than glossed: these are COMMITTED EXPORTS, which may trail those projects' live stores — music_graph's is dated 2026-08-01, and F23 is precisely a case of a committed export being behind. So this reads 'zero in the record I can see', not 'zero in existence'. Six-for-six at zero is still a strong signal, and it would take only one consumer starting to record findings to overturn it.
